fine_trace.code: while (fgets(thisline + readbytes, linesize - readbytes, f) != NULL) {
fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled configuration bytes from the PoC file are read via fgets into the heap-allocated line buffer `thisline`; the first line of the input begins with a NUL byte, making the line appear empty to strlen().
strlen() stops at the leading NUL byte and returns 0, so end == line: the end pointer coincides with the start of the line buffer.

The trailing-linefeed guard dereferences *(end-1) only when end-line == linesize-1 (2047). For an empty line end-line is 0, so the guard short-circuits, does not inspect *(end-1), and provides no protection for the empty-line case.

Root cause: the trailing-LF kill writes through end-1 without first ensuring the line is non-empty (end > line). When end == line, end-1 points one byte before the start of the heap buffer `thisline`, so the write is executed out of bounds.
Sink: heap-buffer-overflow — a NUL byte is written at thisline-1, one byte before the malloc'ed LINESIZE buffer, which ASan reports as an out-of-bounds write of size 1.

issue_alignment.description: Heap overflow in cfgparse when processing an empty configuration line: readcfgfile dereferences end-1 even when end == line, accessing memory one byte before the start of the line buffer without ensuring the line is non-empty.
